description:
Diverse Perspectives. Shared Curiosity. One Mission.

We are a team of students from Boston, MA, majoring in Business Economics, Accounting, Law, and Sociology. Through the Space Mission Design Game Challenge, we strive to turn complex mission trade-offs into an immersive experience while challenging ourselves to engage in new realms of knowledge and skills along the way.

We’re looking for curious, motivated teammates to build something ambitious and bring space closer to everyone.
summary:
Our project is an interactive, fictional space mission planning simulator game, designed to educate users regarding the complex factors of space exploration, and the planning stage which is crucial for a successful mission. 

Players are given a set amount of credits to plan, prepare, and allocate resources for a specialized space mission. They must hire a crew, purchase essential supplies of food, water, oxygen, and propulsion to ensure that their crew successfully completes the mission. 

Players choose a mission from the available choices, where each mission presents unique scenarios, circumstances, and objectives which can influence how to allocate credits to succeed. Each mission also has a brief overview regarding destination, objective, duration, budget, preparation deadline, scientific knowledge, crew capacity, and required propulsion, for the player to analyze and make strategic decisions.

Our project addresses the importance of making space science and exploration more accessible and engaging through interactive learning. By placing players in the role of mission planners, they experience the process of the decision-making involved in real space missions and practice critical thinking skills and strategic planning. Overall, we hope to inspire curiosity about space exploration, and teach players about the importance of resource management, problem-solving, and teamwork.
details:
Our project is a space mission planning game where players have to complete a mission with a limited budget and time. We wanted to show that space exploration involves more than just launching a rocket, especially the planning and decisions that happen beforehand.

In the game, players choose equipment and upgrades based on their mission goals while trying to stay within budget, so they will have to decide what is most important and make trade-offs.

We used real NASA mission information as a reference for the options in the game. We built the game in Unity and Perplexity AI to help with coding.

What makes our game different is that players get to make the decisions themselves instead of just watching a rocket launch. Our goal was to make learning about space more interactive and fun, while also showing the consequences of different choices. Throughout development, we focused on keeping the game realistic but still easy to understand. We also worked on making the menus and instructions clear while balancing what we could realistically build and test.

At this stage we added 5 missions which players can do, but in future looking forward to expanding their number. Furthermore, we want to add more components and elements, such as the flight monitoring, during which the player would be able to help the crew with the mission and guide it to the very end.
